{{color box|#dc143c}} {{color box|white}} | mascot = | nickname = Bearcats | yearbook = | athletic_conference = | website = {{URL|https://prhs.pasoschools.org/|Paso Robles High School}} }} '''Paso Robles High School''' (PRHS) is the only [[comprehensive high school]] located in the city of [[Paso Robles, California]]. The school receives its students from Lewis Flamson Junior High School, located in Paso Robles, as well as from the Lillian Larsen School, a public K-8 school in [[San Miguel, San Luis Obispo County, California|San Miguel, California]], Cappy Culver Elementary and Middle School, a public K-8 school in [[Lake Nacimiento, California]], and Pleasant Valley Elementary School, a public K-8 school located in an outlying area of northeastern [[San Luis Obispo County]]. Additionally, the school receives students from private K-8 schools such as Trinity Lutheran School and St. Rose Catholic School, both located in Paso Robles, and some from Santa Lucia School located in [[Templeton, California|Templeton]], California{{Cite web|url=http://www.greatschools.org/california/paso-robles/6802-Paso-Robles-High-School/|title = Explore Paso Robles High in Paso Robles, CA}} == History == The first high school in San Luis Obispo County, Paso Robles High School was built in 1892 and graduated its first senior class in 1896. Constructed with locally made bricks, the stately three-story structure was located at 17th Street and Vine Street, where Marie Bauer Elementary sits now. A decade upon opening, the high school and upper-level auditorium would languish in the aftermath of the [[1906 San Francisco earthquake|San Francisco Earthquake]] in 1906. A new location was built at 24th and Spring Street, and the faulted building was later razed in 1939. In the 1960s, the 24th Street campus was refurbished, with subsequent additions to what later became Flamson Middle School. (By 2003, the [[2003 San Simeon earthquake|San Simeon Earthquake]] rendered the structures unsalvageable, and a new middle school was constructed.) By 1980, the third PRHS campus was built on Niblick Road, where it stands today. However, football games continue at War Memorial Stadium on the Flamson Middle School campus to a faithful attendance of PRHS boosters. Most other competitive sporting events are held on the PRHS campus. Although the school's athletic facilities are somewhat limited, the campus plays host to an extensive agricultural education facility. The school's mascot is the [[Binturong|bearcat]]. Paso Robles High School was ranked #5 in ''[[U.S. News & World Report]]'''s "Best High Schools in the San Luis Obispo, CA Area". == Curriculum == The school boasts strong vocational, agricultural, and college preparatory programs, as well as a limited number of honors and [[Advanced Placement Program|AP]] courses{{cite web | title=Best High Schools in San Luis Obispo, CA Area | website=US News | url=https://www.usnews.com/education/best-high-schools/california/rankings/san-luis-obispo-ca-42020 | access-date=14 July 2023}} in the fields of [[history]]/[[social science]] (honors/AP), [[English language]]/[[literature]] (honors/AP), [[mathematics]] (AP) and [[science]] (AP). Foreign languages offered include [[Spanish language|Spanish]] and [[American Sign Language]]. The school has also maintained the largest [[SkillsUSA]] organization in California for several years, and it is an [[Advancement Via Individual Determination|AVID]] National Demonstration School. == Extracurricular activities == === Athletics === Paso Robles High School was the northernmost high school in the western half of the [[CIF Southern Section]] for decades. In 2016, Paso Robles transferred into the [[CIF Central Section]] along with most schools in [[San Luis Obispo County, California|San Luis Obispo County]] in a bid to reduce travel expenses and to be more regional.{{Cite news |last=Gibson |first=Travis |date=June 20, 2018 |title=SLO County schools will compete in Central Section next year |pages=3B |work=Tribune, The (San Luis Obispo, CA)}} Now playing in the Mountain League as part of the [[Central Coast Athletic Association]], in years past PRHS used to belong to the since-reformed Northern League, [[Los Padres League]] and [[Pac-8 League]] memberships. ===Boys teams=== Football

Stunt === Journalism === Crimson is the award-winning student news magazine of Paso Robles High School. Crimson is the current form of the monthly tabloid newspaper founded in the 1940s named The Crimson Chronicle and originally The Bearcat. Crimson staff members attend national and local journalism conventions and have won recognition in national and statewide competitions for writing, photography, and design. The publication and website are currently advised by Jeff Mount. Many graduates from the program have gone on to careers in journalism, law, communications, and/or design.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} ==Notable alumni== * [[Bo Bonnheim]], Class of 2011, [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State]] offensive lineman{{Cite news |last=Scroggin |first=Joshua D. |date=September 7, 2013 |title=Former Paso standout begins to emerge for Bulldogs – Fresno State head coach DeRuyter praises center Bonnheim for toughness |pages=S1 |work=The San Luis Obispo Tribune}} * [[Jason Botts]], Class of 1998, [[Texas Rangers (baseball)|Texas Rangers]] [[Major League Baseball|MLB]] player{{cite web | url=http://www.ksby.com/news/former-major-leaguer-botts-inspires-kids-in-return-to-paso-robles/#!prettyPhoto/0/ | title=Former Major Leaguer Botts inspires kids in hometown of Paso Robles | publisher=[[KSBY]] | date=September 12, 2012 | access-date=February 22, 2014 | author=Masuda, Andrew}} * [[Ken Buck (American football)|Ken Buck]], Class of 1949, [[New York Giants]] [[1954 NFL draft|1954 draft]] choice/[[Pacific Tigers|Pacific]] Hall of Fame member{{Cite news |last=Nettleship |first=Johnny |date=December 5, 1953 |title=SporTopics |pages=6 |work=San Luis Obispo Telegram-Tribune}} * [[Derrick Jasper]], Class of 2006, [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]]/[[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]] basketball guard{{Cite web |last=Blue |first=J.
